edge_keepout.why: rule-area strips (half-width 0.2) on every outline and cutout edge: the router keeps its copper 0.35 mm off the edge, above the project copper-to-edge 0.3 (route run 42414083566 had 0.23)

copper_keepouts.why: W2 PWRB-R (review F2 of W2 PCB-PWRB-2): every PWR-A cut-out (pwr_a_cutouts) becomes a hole or notch in PWR-B once the MECH lineage writes it into the contract, so no copper may lie in it or closer to it than the project copper-to-edge clearance. Each cut-out rectangle grown by that clearance is a KiCad rule area on all four copper layers (no tracks, vias, pads or zone fills): the Specctra export hands it to the router as a keepout, the zone filler leaves it empty, DRC reports any track, via or pad inside it, and pcb/board_gen.py copper_keepout_audit measures every copper item of the routed board against the rectangles (the board fails on any copper closer than grow_mm). The routed copper of record before W2 PWRB-R had 475 of 1774 segments and 47 of 255 vias inside the rectangles (route run 43273190849, measured by that audit; review F2 counted 482 / 67 on the iteration-1 board)
